criteria.description: Correctly factors out -Phi(s) from the shaped Bellman equation.
Correctly substitutes the guess and confirms the fixed point, noting argmax_a is unchanged.

solutions.fullSolution: V'(s) = -Phi(s) + max_a E_s'{R(s,a,s') + gamma[Phi(s')+V'(s')]}. Substituting V'(s')=V*(s')-Phi(s') gives Phi(s')+V'(s')=V*(s'). So V'(s) = -Phi(s) + max_a E_s'{R(s,a,s')+gamma*V*(s')} = -Phi(s)+V*(s), confirming the guess. Since Phi(s) doesn't depend on a, argmax_a is unchanged. (Independently verified numerically on a random MDP.)

criteria.description: Correctly contrasts cheap parallelizable simulated rollouts with expensive real rollouts.
Correctly connects this to why on-policy requirements are a real bottleneck.

solutions.fullSolution: In simulation, fresh rollouts cost only compute, cheap and parallelizable. On a physical robot, rollouts require real wall-clock time, wear, safety risk, and often supervision, none of which parallelize. An algorithm needing frequently-refreshed on-policy data (rather than reusing a stored buffer) imposes a real-world sample-collection cost dominating practical training time, why so much robot RL trains in simulation first.

criteria.description: Correctly explains i.i.d. noise's self-cancelling jitter.
Correctly explains correlated noise's coherent excursions and the connection to RLEARN-01's coverage principle.

solutions.fullSolution: I.i.d. per-step noise has zero correlation between steps, so effects tend to average out into small self-cancelling jitter rather than genuine excursions. Temporally-correlated noise pushes in a similar direction over several steps before reversing, producing coherent sustained excursions that actually explore new state-space regions per unit of real-robot time, directly RLEARN-01's frequency/state-coverage principle applied to exploration.
